ib-host-group: The Lean uses E0 × H with E0 = ZMod 2 × ZMod 2, written additively, but orders the two coordinates of E0 the other way round: the Lean element ((a,b),h) is the text's (b,a,h). The text follows the order of the signs of G_Φ in Definition hf-frame. So the split subgroup Ψ_H is the Lean's PhiSet (InPhi g ↔ g.1.1 = 0), σ is sgc0 = ((1,0),0), c is cconj = ((1,1),0), π_t is partner t, and χ_C is chC. The bijection π_t from the complement of Ψ_H onto Ψ_H is partner_bijection.
ib-host-group-fields: The identification of Gal(E/Q) = G0 × A with E0 × A is the homomorphism toE (RecH.lean), which sends the second sign (the character chD) to the Lean's first E0 coordinate, that is to the text's e_2. The assertions of the remark are HostAx.galE_mem_Psi_iff (the subgroup Ψ = Frame.Psi fixes √-d), HostDer.conj_iff (ι is complex conjugation) and HostDer.inertia_d (inertia at d is {1, ι_d}); the statement about inert primes follows from these and Lemma ib-host-arithmetic-data.
ib-arithmetic-data: The data are the structure ArithData (fields q1, d, inertia, frob) and the conditions are the Prop HostFactsS D S. There is a second set of conditions, HostFacts, which also asks that q1 be an odd prime different from d and takes S = {2, q1}; the balance identity is proved under both (colour_balance and ch_balance), and the downstream argument uses HostFactsS, under which q1 need not be prime. The plan's informal statement described the HostFacts form. ψ(n) is primVal D ψ n, a product of cosetMean.
ib-host-chebyshev: This is GPsi D ell ψ: Gz for ψ = 0 (the trivial character in additive notation) and the twisted sum plus y·ell ψ otherwise. Chapter 2 writes G for Gz. The notation g_ψ (rather than G_ψ, which Chapter 2 uses for the weighted sum of a cyclic level) follows Chapter 2's g_χ.
ib-inert-sums: ASK is ASK D N a t w = Σ_{p ≤ N inert} 2 log p · askP + log d · askD; MAIN and De are the definitions of the same names and are complex-valued because ell is. That the inner sum at d has one term is double_coset_singleton (stated there under HostFacts; its proof uses only the description of I_d).
ib-prime-power-orthogonality: Same as the Lean (OrthoRam). It holds for any ArithData, without the conditions of Definition ib-arithmetic-data.
ib-inert-expansion: Same as the Lean lemma askExp (namespace Deduction.CharacterBalance), stated under HostFactsS. Its proof uses sum_vonMangoldt_primePow, orthogonality_ramified and the local lemmas lunram, lsplit and ld; the parallel lemma characterSum_expansion proves the HostFacts version.
ib-truncation: The lemma combines sum_cut (truncation at a/W) and inner_eq (rescaling to GPsi). Both hold for any ArithData.
ib-balance-identity: Same as the Lean, as a complex identity. The proof follows ch_balance: askExp, then sum_cut and inner_eq for each g and ψ, then colour_sum (the sum of a character over the complement of Ψ_H) and PB.sum_partner (π_t is a bijection). The plan's informal statement listed q1 and d as odd primes, which is the HostFacts form; ch_balance assumes HostFactsS.

Data has two further fields, logGam and Ta, which no hypothesis or conclusion used here mentions; they enter earlier variants of the inequality (MeanBoundSecondForm).
ib-comparison-quantities: The Lean names are: s, uF = s^+ − s, Main, Lam5 = 𝓛, Lo5 = Lo, LoP = Lo_max, EDiv = E_Div, Vvar = V, MLo5 = overline Lo, UBar5 = Ū, ErrX5at = Err, logOm = log Ω, ph = φ. ib-comparison-hypotheses: SizeData₂ D C Xpp is the conjunction HidaSetting ∧ DIV ∧ EComp5 ∧ HComp ∧ Count5 ∧ Slopes ∧ QuotientSlopeBoundsWith ∧ LossBounds ∧ SlopeIneq ∧ HHBound ∧ FParams, which are (H1)–(H11) in order. ib-slope-of-n-lower: Same as s_lower5, with K_5 = K5v5. The Lean takes all of (H7) as a hypothesis and uses its second inequality.

ib-comparison-inequality: each_unit_bound_statement proves PointwiseBoundVariant D C Xpp, which is the statement here: SizeData₂'s eleven hypotheses imply ASK u0 ≤ Main u0 + ErrX5at u0 for every u0. The proof follows the Lean: key_identity5 (Step 1), Ga_bound5 (Steps 2 to 4, with phi_bound for Step 3) and weighted_mean_lower_bound_le (Step 5). The same file proves averaged forms (weighted_mean_bound_statement, uniform_bound_statement), which the window bound does not use.
ib-two-measurements: Expository. The attributions of (H2), (H7), (H8) and (H9) to Chapters 5, 7, 8 and 9 follow the plan of those chapters; this chapter uses only the numerical hypotheses.
ib-size-windows: (W1)–(W3) are SizesA (restricted, as in the Lean, to u0 ∈ A0), (W4) is ThinScales, (W5) is CostWindows x (fPl H) b η θ with fPl H = |PhiSet| = |Ψ_H| = 2|H|, and (W6) is RestSize. Thickness is IsThickAt T2 u0 ρ, i.e. ρ ∈ {thickPl (s + u0) : s ∈ T2}, with thickPl h = ((0,1),h) in the Lean's coordinates, which is (1,0,h) here, the element τ_2(h) of Definition hf-frame. β is errorBracketSizeWindows, whose last term the Lean writes as n_2kbx^ε/(n·(n·x^{−ε})).

ib-weight-lipschitz: lipschitz_weight_all proves LipWAll; the two cases are AN.lip_char and AN.lip_triv. Chebyshev's bound is used as sum_vM_le (Σ_{n≤Y} Λ(n) ≤ 3Y).
ib-chebyshev-lipschitz: derivative_integral_all proves DerivIntAll (there is C_d ≥ 0 with DerivInt D ell C_d for all H, D, ell). Part (1) is AN.deriv_char, using mertens_upper; part (2) is zetaPrimeSumErrorLipschitz, proved interval by interval (lip_piece, lip_upto) with Lipschitz constant log 4 + 7 on [1/2, ∞).

Θ is CharacterBalanceMoves.Th with y = A/b; the description of the thick places in the complement of Ψ_H is thick_filter.
ib-kept-character-sum: This is one_char, which takes the derivative bound DerivInt D ell C_d as a hypothesis (supplied in the proof of ch_core by derivative_integral_all). v(ψ) is vv Kp D ell c x ψ, and Σ_ψ v(ψ) = GmA − SigA is sum_vv.

ib-window-bound-shape: Expository; it describes Steps 2 and 3 of the proof of ch_core.
ib-host-arithmetic-data: hostFactsS proves HostFactsS (arith H) (insert H.q H.small), and the set insert H.q H.small is the set of prime factors of Q_S·q. The data arith H are cftData q d (recH H), with recH = toE ∘ art; the Frobenius element is the Artin image of frobUnit and the inertia group the image of localUnits. The proof uses HostDer.art_ch (the d-sign of an Artin image is a Jacobi symbol), HostRaw.QS_split, HostHyp (which includes (−d/q) = 1 and d ≡ 7 mod 16) and HostRaw.art_d.

The first two items are proved inside its proof (hval, via primitive_value_primitive, and hone, via the surjectivity HostDer.art_surj). χ_ψ is H.prim (chr φ ψ). The plan's informal statement gave every nontrivial character the weight (3o+1)^{-1}; the Lean, like Definition wl-weighted-sum, gives the exceptional character weight 1. The proof uses chr_bij, prim_inj, the host conditions kept and ps, the private lemma gmA_eq_triv (characters in X^+ trivial on A are 1 and psC, the first sign θ_q), and prim_read.

Hypothesis (1) is EFamC and hypothesis (2) is ChebyshevInequalityOnFamilyWindows.
